Adding wind cuts solar + battery storage power costs nearly 20%

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Solar and battery storage can do a lot of the heavy lifting in a renewable electricity system.
  • Wind fills gaps when solar output drops, so the system needs fewer batteries to keep electricity flowing.
  • Ember’s analysis, produced with the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), found that adding wind to solar and battery storage cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105 to $86 per megawatt-hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solar and battery storage can do a lot of the heavy lifting in a renewable electricity system. Add wind, and supplying reliable power gets nearly 20% cheaper, according to latest analysis from energy think tank Ember.

Wind fills gaps when solar output drops, so the system needs fewer batteries to keep electricity flowing.

Ember’s analysis, produced with the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), found that adding wind to solar and battery storage cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105 to $86 per megawatt-hour.

The median cost of solar and wind power covering all demand is $89/MWh, with batteries and a little backup.

It has been revealed that solar and wind don’t follow the same schedule. Their output varies by time of day and across seasons, allowing one to offset the other’s shortfalls.

That matters because storing enough electricity to get through a long stretch of weak solar output gets expensive. Wind reduces the amount of energy the batteries need to store in the first place.

In the US, adding wind reduces the modeled battery requirement to meet 90% of demand from 20 hours of electricity use to 12 hours. Europe sees the same reduction, while China’s requirement falls from 18 hours to 12.

The savings also put cheaper renewable power within reach of more regions. With wind included, regions that account for 75% of global electricity demand can meet 90% of their electricity demand at less than $100/MWh. With solar and batteries alone, that share is only 50%.

“We already know that solar and wind are cheap,” said Daan Walter, principal at Ember.

By combining solar, wind, and batteries, we can deliver reliable power at remarkably low costs almost everywhere in the world. That’s a pretty fundamental shift in the economics of energy.

Industry observers note that the researchers also looked at prolonged periods of low output. Globally, weighted by electricity demand, a week of low solar output occurs roughly four times a year. A week in which both solar and wind output are low occurs only about once every four years.

That’s a global average, so individual locations will have different experiences. Ember defines a lull as seven consecutive days of output below half the source’s average.

Combining wind and solar reduces the gaps in low output.

The findings also raise questions for developers planning newly introduced fossil fuel plants.

Ember identifies 845 GW of coal and gas capacity in planning worldwide. Adding wind raises the share located in regions where solar, wind, and battery storage can meet 90% of demand for under $100/MWh from 71% to 90%.

In China alone, wind brings another 91 GW of planned coal and gas capacity into the range where renewables are cheaper.

Industry observers note that include backup to cover all demand, and 706 GW of the planned fossil fuel capacity sits in regions where the renewable-based alternative costs less than $100/MWh. Without wind, that figure falls to 520 GW.

For investors financing fossil fuel plants in the pipeline that are expected to run for decades, there is likely already a cheaper renewable alternative available to meet the same electricity demand, so it’s worth scrutinizing the project’s economics.

Good way to think about the whole system. So what exactly does Don not-Quixote have against windmills?

Ember’s interactive Wind + Solar + Battery Atlas lets people explore reliable electricity costs in their own region.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that EVERYBODY LOVE YOGURT.
  • In a recent development, "Most of the world is lactose intolerant and has been for thousands and thousands of years," says Robert Hutkins, PhD, a professor of food microbiology at the University of Nebraska.
  • Whether you need help digesting lactose or not, the latest research suggests that yogurt has wide-ranging benefits, from enhancing gut health to improving blood sugar control to maybe even reducing your risk of an early death.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that EVERYBODY LOVE YOGURT. Okay, maybe not everyone, but there's a reason yogurt has been a dietary staple in dozens of countries for centuries. Yogurt doesn't spoil as fast as milk, yet still delivers milk's nutrients—protein, calcium, potassium, magnesium—without the same risk of, um, certain GI issues.

In a recent development, "Most of the world is lactose intolerant and has been for thousands and thousands of years," says Robert Hutkins, PhD, a professor of food microbiology at the University of Nebraska. "Humans figured out that even if they were lactose intolerant, they could still consume cultured milks because the culture helps degrade the lactose before it gets to the colon and gets fermented by gas-producing microbes.".

Whether you need help digesting lactose or not, the latest research suggests that yogurt has wide-ranging benefits, from enhancing gut health to improving blood sugar control to maybe even reducing your risk of an early death.

From Europe to Asia to Africa, all yogurt starts with the same basic ingredients: milk and good bacteria. But no two types are exactly alike. Here's what to know before your next grocery run.

Traditional Greek yogurt is strained through a cheesecloth to remove excess fluid. Yogurt factories use centrifuges or special filters instead. What's left behind is a thick, smooth yogurt with a slightly acidic flavor and a concentrated source of nutrients, including about 18 grams of protein per 6-ounce container.

According to recent reports, some food makers add thickeners as a shortcut, so check the label for a simple ingredient list of milk, cream, and yogurt cultures. "The products with thickeners added have a different texture, a little bit more gumminess," says Molly Kimball, RD, CSSD, a dietitian based in Louisiana. Swap in Greek yogurt for sour cream or mayo, or stir it into guacamole—the lactic acid slows down the oxidation that turns avocados brown.

Technically considered a soft cheese, skyr is strained like Greek yogurt to produce something firm yet creamy. It's usually made with skim milk, yielding yogurt with slightly more protein than Greek yogurt: about 19 grams of protein per 6 ounces. Use skyr to make dips hearty enough to stand up to cut vegetables (or chips). Or stir it into bolognese to impart a velvety texture and an extra boost of protein.

Recent findings suggest that this yogurt variety isn't strained, so it has a thinner texture and less protein than its Greek or Icelandic cousins: about 6 grams per 6 ounces. Traditional Bulgarian yogurt gets its signature sharp flavor from high concentrations of the aptly named Lactobacillus Bulgaricus bacteria, which produce lactic acid. Kimball recommends blending Bulgarian yogurt into smoothies to add a tanginess that counterbalances sweeter ingredients.

Most yogurts are fermented in large vats. As yogurt bacteria digest milk, they produce a wide variety of metabolites, including gel-like substances called exopolysaccharides. Then the yogurt is pumped into the smaller containers we snag at the grocery store.

Sources indicate that with French-style yogurt, the milk and bacterial cultures are poured into cups earlier, before the microbes multiply. "That gives you a more custardy product because it hasn't gone through this pumping phase that disturbs the gel," states Hutkins. Inside a 6-ounce cup of French-style yogurt, you'll find about 5 grams of protein. To try it the French way, eat your yogurt for dessert, alone or paired with a little honey or jam.

This tangy, thin, pourable yogurt is fermented with kefir grains–gelatinous clusters that contain milk proteins and up to 50 bacterial and yeast species. During fermentation, these yeasts can leave behind traces of alcohol and carbon dioxide, or fizz. However, many mass-produced kefirs use standardized starter cultures instead to maintain consistent product quality and keep the alcohol concentration low enough to sell in grocery stores.

It has been revealed that kimball suggests drinking plain kefir, Russian or otherwise. It packs about 8 grams of protein per cup. If you can't handle the sour flavor, balance it with a teaspoon or less of maple syrup or a few drops of stevia or monk fruit. If you want a flavored variety, pick one with no more than 5 grams of added sugar.

Sweet and mildly acidic, dahi is the key ingredient in Indian staples like lassi–a yogurt drink often flavored with mango, spices, or rosewater–and raita, the sauce that cools your mouth when you order your vindaloo extra hot. Some dahi varieties contain Leuconostoc, bacteria that produce a metabolite called diacetyl that imparts a buttery flavor. Each six-ounce serving of dahi packs about 7 grams of protein.

Drinkable like kefir, laban is sour but smooth and contains about 5 grams of protein per six ounces. Strain it in a colander or cheesecloth to make labneh, a thick, soft, yogurt-like cheese traditionally smeared on sandwiches and stacked on mezze platters.

Sources indicate that this drinkable yogurt is often thicker than fermented milk beverages. Its mix of cultures, which hail mostly from the Lactobacillusgenus, imparts a moderately acidic flavor with subtle buttery notes. Amasi packs about 6 grams of protein per six ounces. It's traditionally eaten with maize or sorghum porridge, especially at breakfast.

Julie Stewart is a writer and content strategist whose work has also appeared in Health, and Women’s Health, Everyday Health, Vice, and Shape.

Industry observers note that december options still priced protection against a fall, though at a discount to comparable bets on a rise, and traders may still move prices as they adjust hedges around settlement. Whether the rally lasts depends on demand for Bitcoin after those contracts expire.

A bounce as Friday’s contracts roll off would leave the question of spot demand returning for Bitcoin unanswered.

Sources indicate that as of Nov. 26, GEX Monitor found that the premium for comparable Friday Bitcoin puts over calls had shrunk to 0.18 volatility points from 13.71 in its previous daily reading.

Industry observers note that puts offer protection against a fall, while calls give traders exposure to a rise. By Thursday morning, the two sides were priced almost evenly on that measure for Friday’s expiry.

According to recent reports, comparable puts carried premiums of 5.82 volatility points for Dec. 4, 8.10 for Dec. 11 and 6.62 for Dec. 25. All three premiums narrowed from the prior snapshot, yet each remained far wider than Friday’s.

Industry observers note that an OptimistFi snapshot highlighted the same pattern, with Friday’s put premium near 0.2 points and the Dec. 11 and Dec. 25 premiums at 6.4 and 6.9 points.

December puts kept a larger premium over comparable calls in the Nov. 26 options snapshot.

Of the four expiries shown, the Nov. 27 premium narrowed the most.

According to recent reports, the two observations measure relative implied volatility. They do not measure options cash premiums, completed hedge flows or the probability of a price drop.

According to recent reports, compare GEX Monitor observations from Nov. 25 at 08:14 UTC and Nov. 26 at 08:10 UTC. The display shows put implied volatility minus comparable call implied volatility for 25-delta options, the opposite sign from the reported risk reversal. Positions on the common axis use the values as published to two decimals.

It has been revealed that the two observations measure relative implied volatility. They do not measure options cash premiums, completed hedge flows or the probability of a price drop.

Annualized implied volatility for Friday's options with strikes near Bitcoin’s price fell from 59.04% to 43.03% for Nov. 27, a drop of 16.01 volatility points. For Dec. 25, it fell from 51.17% to 48.21%, just 2.96 points.

PerpFinder’s expiry calendar revealed over $6.8 billion of Bitcoin inverse options and $629.2 million of Ethereum inverse options due to settle at 08:00 UTC on Nov. 27.

The payout depends on where the settlement price lands relative to each contract’s strike.

Deribit’s inverse options settle financially in Bitcoin or Ethereum, depending on the contract. An option that finishes out of the money expires worthless, while an in-the-money contract pays out its intrinsic value, converted into the settlement coin.

As an option near the current price approaches expiry, even a small move can change how much a dealer needs to buy or sell to offset risk. After settlement, participants can unwind those hedges or replace them if they roll into a later expiry.

A study by Dustin Weiss and co-authors found intraday Bitcoin price reversals around past Deribit expiries. The reversal was most pronounced when open interest was concentrated near the prevailing price, and estimated dealer positioning was consistent with buying into rises and selling into declines to stay hedged.

Trading activity also rose in Deribit perpetual futures and the spot venues used for settlement.

Industry observers note that the Dec. 11 maturity was carrying $717.1 million in Bitcoin inverse-options open interest in PerpFinder’s Thursday collection, and falls after the Federal Reserve’s Dec. 8-9 policy meeting.

It has been revealed that further out, PerpFinder’s Thursday tally indicated $10 billion in Bitcoin inverse-options open interest for Dec. 25, about 47% more than Friday’s Bitcoin-only expiry. It gives December its own large settlement to watch alongside the higher relative price of its puts.

Industry observers note that farside Investors recorded over $3 billion of net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs across seven consecutive trading sessions through Nov. 25, including $453 million in the last session.

It has been revealed that daily net flows for US spot Bitcoin ETFs tracked by Farside Investors, Nov. 17-25.

According to recent reports, bitfinex’s Nov. 25 analysis described how rapidly an earlier rebound faded. After a Nov. 21 low near $55,500, Bitcoin reached $64,673 on Nov. 23 and gave back its intraday gain, finishing near $61,300.

A recovery that holds beyond the settlement window, a turn toward ETF inflows and a continued narrowing of December’s put premiums would give buyers a fuller picture.

ETF inflows would show demand returning through the funds, and cheaper December puts would show the change in options pricing had spread beyond Friday.

Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

According to recent reports, in a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, said it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

The development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

Recent findings suggest that the Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

In a recent development, as of the latest update by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are at the moment being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Update Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Recent findings suggest that protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Revision Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Patch Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP.

Ripple’s expansion alone won’t send XRP to $10, a popular wealth coach states.

A $10 XRP would imply a circulating market value of roughly $630 billion, not simply another rally on Ripple announcements.

Industry observers note that that is the central argument from Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, a wealth coach whose latest YouTube video episode examines why the company’s institutional expansion has not translated into the token price many holders expected.

It has been revealed that using approximately 63 billion XRP in circulation, Stevenson argues that reaching that XRP valuation requires more than partnerships and regulatory milestones. It requires sustained demand to own the token, rather than merely move money through it.

Stevenson separates Ripple’s corporate performance, adoption of its products, demand for XRP and the token’s market price. Those categories overlap, but they are not interchangeable: a customer using Ripple’s custody services or stablecoin does not necessarily need XRP.

Recent findings suggest that even payments routed through XRP may generate limited lasting demand. In the process she describes, a payment provider buys the token, transfers it and sells it into the destination currency within seconds, allowing the same inventory to support repeated transactions.

“Significant payment numbers alone don’t automatically push the price up,” Dr. Stevenson says. The more consequential question is how much XRP participants need to keep available between transactions.

According to recent reports, market makers may hold inventory to support larger payment flows, creating a potential link between usage and ownership. Still, the video does not quantify how much additional inventory those flows would require.

Industry observers note that dr. Kamilah Stevenson cites roughly 1.19 billion XRP held by ETFs and about 473 million held by Evernorth, a company established to accumulate XRP. Those are figures presented in the video, rather than independently verified current totals.

Her distinction is useful: XRP-backed fund holdings represent direct token ownership, while the national trust bank approval she attributes to Ripple does not itself require institutions to purchase XRP.

Supply remains part of the calculation. Stevenson puts Ripple’s escrow holdings at around 31 billion XRP, with up to one billion released monthly and unused amounts returned to escrow. An unlock is therefore not equivalent to an immediate market sale.

Recent findings suggest that the sharper test is whether an announcement creates incremental buying, how long those tokens stay held and whether newly introduced supply offsets that demand. Dr. Stevenson remains bullish, but the adoption figures she discusses do not establish when XRP reaches $10.

Switzerland is bringing Bitcoin self-custody into a global crypto tax reporting network

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 25, Switzerland’s Federal Council approved 57 potential partners for automatic exchanges of crypto tax information with Switzerland, so a Bitcoin withdrawal from a covered Swiss exchange to a hardware wallet could show up in an annual tax report.
  • The list includes every EU member state, the UK, and several G20 jurisdictions.
  • The rules are part of the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on Nov. 25, Switzerland’s Federal Council approved 57 potential partners for automatic exchanges of crypto tax information with Switzerland, so a Bitcoin withdrawal from a covered Swiss exchange to a hardware wallet could show up in an annual tax report.

The list includes every EU member state, the UK, and several G20 jurisdictions. Switzerland plans to start exchanging data in 2028 with partners that want to participate and meet the OECD’s confidentiality, data security, and other requirements.

The rules are part of the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Under the OECD standard, providers must retain the addresses tied to certain outbound transfers for at least five years so tax authorities can ask for them later.

Suppose a customer whose activity is subject to reporting withdraws 1 BTC from a covered Swiss exchange to a hardware wallet.

Under the outbound transfer rule, if the exchange doesn’t know the destination to be associated with a crypto service provider or a financial institution, the transfer can add 1 BTC and its fair market value in regular currency at the time of the transfer, net of transaction fees, to the customer’s annual outbound totals.

The reporting framework accounts for each relevant asset separately, so Bitcoin and other assets have their own totals.

Sources indicate that A transfer to an address the exchange knows is associated with a crypto service provider or financial institution falls outside that field, though other transfer rules can still apply. A wallet the customer already controls can fall within the external-wallet rule.

It has been revealed that say the customer bought Bitcoin on the same exchange before withdrawing it. A qualifying purchase can appear in the report under the purchase category, and a qualifying withdrawal can appear in the transfer totals.

What a covered provider sends and what it keeps under the OECD framework.

Under CARF, tax authorities can request a destination address separately from the annual report.

Applies to qualifying outbound transfers of relevant crypto assets for reportable customers to destinations the provider does not know to be associated with a virtual asset service provider or financial institution. Exchange with foreign partners depends on activation and eligibility. The five-year label is the OECD minimum.

In a recent development, maps OECD CARF Section II(A)(3)(i) and Section III(D)(3) alongside Article 15 of the Swiss tax information exchange act. Arrows show the route of information.

In a recent development, applies to qualifying outbound transfers of relevant crypto assets for reportable customers to destinations the provider does not know to be associated with a virtual asset service provider or financial institution. Exchange with foreign partners depends on activation and eligibility. The five-year label is the OECD minimum.

The reporting framework pairs transaction data with identifying information. Subject to the applicable exceptions, that information includes a customer’s name, mailing address, tax residence, taxpayer identification number and, for individuals, date of birth.

The transaction fields cover qualifying purchases, sales, swaps and transfers.

The automatic report covers transactions the provider handles, so later movements between two private wallets without the provider’s involvement fall outside that provider’s report. The required fields omit private keys, seed phrases and full self-custody wallet balances.

Recent findings suggest that swiss law sets a longer retention period for covered compliance records. Article 17a of the Federal Act on the International Automatic Exchange of Information in Tax Matters requires covered providers to keep records and supporting documents created or obtained to meet their CARF and Swiss statutory obligations.

It refers to Article 958f of the Swiss Code of Obligations, which sets a ten-year retention period.

The Federal Council’s explanation of the legislation confirms the ten-year Swiss period when discussing CARF recordkeeping. Article 17a defines covered records by their role in meeting the provider’s obligations. It does not spell out how the ten-year period applies to individual wallet addresses.

Switzerland’s legal basis for crypto information exchange took effect Jan. 1, 2026. Its State Secretariat for International Finance says the crypto provisions do not apply in 2026 and that Jan. 1, 2027 is the earliest implementation date.

Sources indicate that under the Swiss filing rule, reporting providers have six months after the relevant calendar year ends to submit their reports to the Federal Tax Administration. The Swiss authority then forwards the information to eligible foreign counterparts under the applicable agreement.

If implementation begins in 2027, providers would collect that year’s data and submit it in 2028, when the first cross-border exchanges are planned.

Recent findings suggest that for a reportable customer, a qualifying transfer in the first collection year could be in the record before anything is sent abroad. Keeping the withdrawal date, amount, and destination alongside the exchange record can help reconcile that transfer with other activity involving the same Bitcoin.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month.
  • The Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging.
  • When Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk noted it wouldn’t even have a plug.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month. But there’s a problem buyers should know about: they won’t be able to charge it at home.

The Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging. And the wireless home charging pad Tesla has been teasing since 2023 still isn’t something you can buy.

When Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk noted it wouldn’t even have a plug. “It just goes over the inductive charger and charges,” he said on stage.

That initiative didn’t survive production, or at least the current version in production. Cybercabs have a NACS charge port behind a panel in the rear bumper, and Tesla has been plugging Cybercabs into regular Superchargers in Austin since they joined the fleet.

In a recent development, the bigger concern is what sits behind that port. Tesla confirmed to attendees at Tesla’s Austin launch event in September that Cybercab has no onboard charger, the box that turns the AC power coming out of your wall into DC power the battery can store.

Sources indicate that no onboard charger means no Wall Connector. No Mobile Connector on a 120V outlet, and no Level 2 station at the mall either. If it isn’t a DC fast charger, the Cybercab can’t use it.

For a robotaxi, deleting the onboard charger makes sense. It’s one less part to buy, cool, and carry around, and a fleet car spends its downtime at a depot, not in someone’s garage. Those little things help make the car more economical and efficient.

But Tesla is now selling the Cybercab to individuals.

As we reported last week, Tesla’s Cybercab autonomy agreement requires a $299 monthly subscription for the car to move at all. The same document puts charging squarely on the buyer: “You are responsible for registration, insurance, parking, charging, general cleaning and all other costs.”.

It also tells owners to “keep the vehicle charged and connected so over-the-air updates can install.” Connected to what, it doesn’t say.

The Cybercab Order Agreement limits the car to NACS DC fast charging, Superchargers included. It also says only the registered owner can use the Cybercab, and only while physically present in it for the entire trip.

The subscription agreement carves out one exception: when service is due, the Cybercab “will travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center.” Nothing similar exists for charging.

Industry observers note that so you can’t send your Cybercab to a Supercharger at 2 a.m. while you sleep, which is the one thing a self-driving car should be great at. You’d have to ride along, sit in a two-seater at a Supercharger while it charges, and ride back home.

The obvious answer is the wireless home charger Tesla keeps promising.

Tesla first indicated what looked like a wireless home charging station during its Investor Day in March 2023. Later that year, chief designer Franz von Holzhausen confirmed the project on Jay Leno’s Garage, saying owners would “just drive over the pad in your garage” to start charging.

Tesla then filed patents for the charging pad and, after the Cybercab unveiling, released a video of it charging the robotaxi at 25 kW, claiming efficiency “well above 90%.” In February, the FCC granted Tesla a waiver to use ultra-wideband radios to guide the Cybercab onto the pad.

It has been revealed that and that’s where it stops. Tesla has never sold the pad, never priced it, and never given it a launch date. It even gave up on wireless charging for the Cybertruck last year, even though the truck shipped with the connectors for it.

With deliveries estimated for December, Tesla has about six weeks to launch a home pad if it wants the first owners to charge in their own garage.

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s own looks for Cybercab charging revolve around fleet depots. In Austin, it filed plans for a hub on St. Elmo Road with 48 V4 Supercharger stalls in a first phase and cabinets to support 80 wireless chargers in a second.

Sources indicate that tesla could, in theory, let private owners use it. But with the owner-presence rule, that means riding to a depot across town and waiting there. That’s a Supercharger visit with extra steps.

Industry observers note that the other route is a home DC charger, and those exist. We covered Sigenergy’s 25 kW bidirectional DC charging module last year, which bypasses a car’s onboard charger the same way a Supercharger does. Lunar Energy also declared a 25 kW home DC charger this year, but it’s not expected until mid-2027.

Neither is a plug-and-play answer. Sigenergy’s module is built to sit inside its SigenStor home battery system, which isn’t cheap, and Tesla would have to support third-party DC charging on a car it controls this tightly. Tesla could also build its own small DC wall unit. It hasn’t unveiled one, but CEO Elon Musk talked about integrating one into the Powerwall for years.

This is what happens when you take a vehicle designed for a fleet and sell it to consumers to hit a deadline. And let’s be honest, charging is probably not even in the top 5 of problems with selling the Cybercab to personal owners in its current state.

Industry observers note that musk promised a Cybercab would be sold to a customer for under $30,000 before 2027. Technically, he’s going to make it. But on the Q3 earnings call, he also remarked “the vast majority” of Cybercabs will stay Tesla-owned and run as transport-as-a-service. The car was clearly engineered around that, and deleting the onboard charger is the best example.

In a recent development, that saved Tesla money on every unit. The cost now lands on the few people buying one.

It has been revealed that I don't see any evidence that the production Cybercab has the onboard hardware to use such a pad. Besides the wireless receiver coil it would need some kind of charging hardware to convert the pulsed wireless charging into DC to charge the battery.

Recent findings suggest that if you live in Austin next to a Supercharger, you’ll manage. But think about what Tesla is actually selling here: a self-driving car that can’t drive itself to charge, can’t charge in your garage, and needs you sitting in it at a Supercharger. That’s worse than owning a Model 3 with a Wall Connector, and it costs $299 a month on top.

Recent findings suggest that the fix exists in Tesla’s labs. It has the pad, the patents, and the FCC approval. It needs to ship it as a product, ideally bundled with the car, or change the contract to let the Cybercab go charge on its own.

Recent findings suggest that will the first Cybercab owners get a wireless pad in December, or will they spend their evenings at Superchargers? And if it releases, how much will it cost? The rare few home wireless chargers that have been sold to date have been quite expensive, and the value proposition of the Cybercab, which is currently basically a $300 a month lease with a $30,000 down payment, is already pretty awful.

Latest Update: The 21 Best Adam Driver Movies, Ranked

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that LET’S RAPIDLY CUT to the chase: Adam Driver is a good actor.
  • Some may still think of Driver, who this month teams up with director James Gray for one of his best roles ever in the crime drama Paper Tiger, as Adam Sackler, the overly emotional Brooklyn boyfriend of Lena Dunham in Girls (a role for which he was nominated for three Emmys).
  • Industry observers note that driver has emerged in recent years as someone who works almost exclusively with elite, top-notch directors, headlining projects from the likes of Scorsese and Michael Mann as well as Spike Lee and Ridley Scott (just to name a few).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that LET’S RAPIDLY CUT to the chase: Adam Driver is a good actor. That’s probably an understatement to say the least; if Martin Scorsese, of all people, refers to someone as “one of the finest, if not the finest actor of his generation,” well, then, yeah, they’re probably pretty good.

Some may still think of Driver, who this month teams up with director James Gray for one of his best roles ever in the crime drama Paper Tiger, as Adam Sackler, the overly emotional Brooklyn boyfriend of Lena Dunham in Girls (a role for which he was nominated for three Emmys). But while he was obviously stellar in his breakthrough role on HBO’s hit comedy, it’s clear that he’s come a significant way in the time since first coming through to the public consciousness.

Industry observers note that driver has emerged in recent years as someone who works almost exclusively with elite, top-notch directors, headlining projects from the likes of Scorsese and Michael Mann as well as Spike Lee and Ridley Scott (just to name a few). He frequently shows his comedy (or, maybe dramedy) chops working with Noah Baumbach.

He’s also, of course, earned his presence on the blockbuster scene: while opinions abound with regard to the Star Wars sequel trilogy, it’d be hard for anyone to deny the intensity with which Driver dominates the screen as the main villain of those films.

According to recent reports, for someone whose film career has only been going for about a decade, Driver has a remarkable resume and, having been nominated for a pair of Oscars already, accomplished a huge amount. As he continues to add more and more exciting projects to his ledger—he’s recently joined the cast of Marvel’s new X-Men movie— we wanted to rank the very best roles Driver has had so far.

Here are the best films of Adam Driver, ranked.

In one of his first leading roles, Driver gave audiences a taste of the intense leading man he would eventually become as one half of a deeply troubled couple (with a newborn child) in Hungry Hearts.

One thing we haven’t gotten enough of—in the post-Girls era—is Driver showing off his full comedy chops. In What If, a rom-com where he stars alongside Daniel Radcliffe, Zoe Kazan, and Mackenzie Davis, he gets to have a whole lot of fun as a romantic co-lead (and yell about having sex and eating nachos).

According to recent reports, white Noise marked Driver’s fifth collaboration with writer/director Noah Baumbach. And while the movie didn’t wind up getting the Oscar love that it may have aspired for, it still found Driver giving a committed and intense—if deeply strange—performance. Fans of Don DeLillo's book upon which the film is based probably enjoyed what he brought to the table here.

Recent findings suggest that one of the hallmarks of Driver’s recent career is working with as many legendary directors as he can possibly fit into his schedule. That includes three movies with indie king Jim Jarmusch; Father Mother Sister Brother cast Driver as a key piece of a striking ensemble, and delivered one of his most naturalistic and honest recent performances.

According to recent reports, speaking of legendary directors, Driver took the lead in Megalopolis, the maximalist, long-in-the-works sci-fi epic from Francis Ford Coppola (of The Godfather and Apocalypse Now fame), as an urban planner or architect of some sort in a bizarre future world. The movie is kind of a massive disaster, but Driver, as always, brings his all (with some legendary line-readings included). It’s hard to say it’s good, but you certainly can’t look away—and it’s clearly an experience Driver wanted. An important touchstone for his career in any regard.

According to recent reports, megalopolis is not streaming anywhere or available on physical media. You are on your own with this one—if you find it, let me know.

In a movie full of larger-than-life, outrageous characters (and even more outrageous accents), Driver manages to somewhat keep House of Gucci on the rails. He plays Ridley Scott’s Maurizio Gucci, and while he, too, has an absurd accent, it somehow winds up being the most grounded and reasoned performance in the whole film. This movie is camp, but Driver winds up playing it pretty straight—which mostly works.

Driver’s first collaboration with Noah Baumbach came as Lev, a dude who comes in and out of the life of Greta Gerwig’s titular character as she flails her way through her 20s. This light and fun character feels almost like the opposite of Driver’s intense turn in another coming-of-age-in-NYC-story, Girls.

In The Report, Driver plays Daniel Jones, the real-life investigator who led the search into the CIA’s use of torture in the aftermath of 9/11. This gripping true story isn’t one of Driver’s flashiest performances, but it may be his most pertinent to the world we live in today.

Sources indicate that driver made his first—and so far only—appearance in a Coen Brothers film with an ever-so-brief couple of scenes as Al Cody in Inside Llewyn Davis. He makes himself known in those scenes, though, as a gimmicky country music cowboy whose sole job is to say things like “OUUUUTER….. SPAAACEEEEE” on songs intended to be cheap radio hits. Still, Driver gives this character a sense of humanity in offering the titular musician (Oscar Isaac) a place to stay. He’s out of the movie just about as swiftly as he gets into it, but it’s the definition of a scene-stealing turn.

Industry observers note that this movie is weird! Driver plays a problematic stand-up comedian named Henry McHenry (that’s right) who’s married to an opera singer (Marion Cotillard)... and then they have a daughter, who is… a wunderkind musician, and also a marionette puppet. Things go way off the rails from there in a way that we wouldn’t dare spoil, but trust us on this: it’s pretty easily the most bonkers movie on this list.

There’s not much to Paterson—a film about a bus driver who writes poetry—but it’s one of Driver’s most unique and subdued performances, quite the shift for a guy so well known for going significant and intense.

Industry observers note that to play a Jesuit monk in Silence, Martin Scorsese’s long-gestating (but little-seen) 2016 passion project, Driver went full Method, losing nearly 50 pounds in preparation to play the role (according to co-star Andrew Garfield during an interview on The Late Show). This reflects on Driver’s performance, where he’s as intense and dialed in as he’s ever been.

Sources indicate that by teaming up with the legendary Michael Mann (Heat, Collateral, Miami Vice), Driver manages to check yet another iconic director off his list. In this slow burn, brooding drama, Driver plays Enzo Ferrari, a win-at-all-costs businessman and racing team leader who finds himself, in 1957, at a crossroads with regards to both his troubled business and complicated personal/family life. Driver gives a subdued performance that scorches through the screen as the viewer constantly wonders whether he’s pushed one part of his life too far; he gives an Italian accent once again, by the way, and it goes a lot better than it did in House of Gucci.

Driver totally pops in While We’re Young, his second collab with Noah Baumbach. Here, he plays an ambitious and opportunistic Bushwick hipster who, along with his wife (Amanda Seyfried) meets an older couple (Ben Stiller and Naomi Watts) and become their “cool” friends. This movie is a very funny commentary on friendship, careers, and being content with getting older—and Driver’s character (a wannabe documentarian who doesn’t seem to have any sort of moral or ethical code) is a huge highlight.

Sources indicate that rian Johnson brought Kylo Ren to the brink in Star Wars: The Last Jedi, giving Driver’s striking, and, at times, maniacal villain the chance to really set himself apart from others in the franchise. The movie dives into Kylo’s relationship with all sorts of characters, including Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) and Rey (Daisy Ridley), leading to an epic film-ending interaction with the former—and tons of confused fans online wishing he would get together with the latter. The movie leaves Ren in a position where he could have potentially become the most evil and powerful villain the series has ever seen; unfortunately, The Rise of Skywalker squandered all of it.

In a recent development, imagine Steven Soderbergh’s Logan Lucky as the blue-collar version of his Ocean’s trilogy. Driver plays a war veteran bartender (who lost his forearm during a tour of duty) who, along with his brother (Channing Tatum) stage a major heist at a NASCAR racetrack. Driver plays his character as slow, but not a complete idiot—because this movie is far too smart for such 2-D characterizations. An extremely fun movie with a stacked cast.

According to recent reports, teaming up with writer/director Spike Lee to play undercover detective Philip "Flip" Zimmerman in BlacKkKlansman earned Driver his first Oscar nomination, something that even at the time felt overdue—but was very, very deserved. This movie plays strongly on the relationship between Driver and John David Washington, and finds Driver playing, essentially, two characters: his noble detective, and the person he has to become while infiltrating the KKK.

There are a lot of actors out there who reach a certain level of fame and get a little skittish when it comes to playing characters who could even potentially be seen as unsavory. In The Last Duel, Driver gives an absolutely fearless performance as Jacques Le Gris, a 14th-century knight who’s not only unsavory, but absolutely vile. The charm that we’ve gotten so frequently from Driver works to perfection here, as a character who at first invites an air of indifference eventually becomes so disgusting that he’s without question the worse of two evils. The Last Duel spends the duration of its running time asking questions about the truth and how it evolves over time—and while the specifics may be uncertain, the movie makes no mistakes about how heinous this character is (and how perfectly despicable Driver plays him).

Marriage Story brought Driver his second (and most recent) Oscar nomination, and a tidal wave of online memes (you’ve almost certainly seen him punch that wall more times than you’ve actually seen the movie), but his fourth collaboration with Noah Baumbach is probably his most impressive dramatic performance to date. Telling the male side of a dissolved relationship (Scarlett Johansson plays his soon-to-be-ex-wife), Driver finds the perfect mix of charming, charismatic, and delusional in playing Charlie, the man at (one half of) the center of the story.

After 2022’s Armageddon Time, James Gray had another largely autobiographical story to tell in Paper Tiger, this time more in line with his origins as a teller of crime drama stories. While Paper Tiger once again features characters based on Gray’s parents (this time Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, after they were played by Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway in Armageddon Time), it adds a new character named Uncle Gary to the mix, played by Driver. Gary is a brash, lovable former cop, an ambitious businessman who goes around town like he owns the place and brings fancy dinners (shout out Peter Luger!) into his family’s home as a special surprise when he’s got a deal to spring on his brother. Of course, these kinds of deals in movies are never as good as they seem, and everyone winds up in more trouble than they bargained for. Driver plays the character in a gray area, and his plethora of charisma make it one of his very best roles to date. When he’s on screen, you simply can’t look away.

Volkswagen will reveal the new GTI hot hatch on Friday, promising it will be “something really spicy.”.

To celebrate the GTI’s 50th anniversary, Volkswagen is “starting a new chapter,” with its first all-electric model to bear the iconic performance badge.

The ID. Polo GTI “brings the legendary GTI driving pleasure into the electric future,” VW said after opening pre-orders last month.

In a recent development, volkswagen previewed a mysterious newly introduced hot hatch draped under a cloth that appears to be a souped-up version of the ID. Polo GTI. Despite its attempt to “hide” it, you can see the massive rear wing and wide wheel arches under the cloth.

The company promised that “something really spicy” will be served this Friday, November 20, with the tags #Volkswagen, #GTI, and #GTI50.

Although no other details were revealed, the latest hot hatch is thought to be the more powerful “Clubsport” variant.

A post shared by Volkswagen (@volkswagen).

Volkswagen’s head of driving dynamics, Florian Umbach, told Autocar earlier this year that the tech giant is planning to launch the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, a more powerful variant that will deliver close to 300 hp, up from 223 hp in the standard model.

Umbach remarked that Volkswagen is developing “a similar kind of paddleshift power delivery that the Hyundai N cars have” for the upcoming electric hot hatch.

Hyundai’s performance EVs, the IONIQ 5 N and IONIQ 6 N, feature a simulated gear-shifting system called N e-Shift that uses paddle shifters on the steering wheel to replicate the feel of an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. It works with the N Active Sound+ system to make it feel like you’re in a traditional gas-powered sports car.

It has yet to be confirmed whether the hot hatch debuting on Friday is, in fact, the new ID. Polo Clubsport, but the design clues give us a good idea of what’s coming.

Industry observers note that man, $45k for a starting price is a little uncomfortably steep for a hatch, given there are a little bigger options in that range. I wish it started somewhere in the 30s to be competitive.

Check back on Friday for the full details.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000).

Like the first Golf GTI from 1976, the electric ID. Polo GTI uses a front-wheel-drive powertrain. The front-mounted electric motor delivers 223 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft (290 Nm) of instant torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 6.8 seconds.

In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

Industry News: Bitcoin miners are shutting down machines, but mining just got even harder

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that bitcoin's mining difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov.
  • Data from Mempool.space highlighted that the adjustment took effect at 05:17 UTC at block 977,760, raising mining difficulty from 134.82 trillion to 145.09 trillion.
  • Since expected mining rewards per unit of computing power move inversely to difficulty, the increase reduces what Bitcoin miners can expect to earn from their existing machines by 7.08%, assuming average transaction fees remain unchanged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bitcoin's mining difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov. 27, intensifying financial pressure on miners already switching off machines.

Data from Mempool.space highlighted that the adjustment took effect at 05:17 UTC at block 977,760, raising mining difficulty from 134.82 trillion to 145.09 trillion.

Since expected mining rewards per unit of computing power move inversely to difficulty, the increase reduces what Bitcoin miners can expect to earn from their existing machines by 7.08%, assuming average transaction fees remain unchanged.

From a starting price of $60,000, Bitcoin would need to climb approximately 7.61% to $64,570 for miners to restore their previous gross dollar revenue.

Bitcoin mining difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov. 27. The chart holds hashrate and block rewards fixed.

At unchanged fees, the modeled price rise of about 7.61% would restore expected gross mining revenue to its pre-reset level.

Illustrative expected gross revenue per unit of hashrate. The comparison holds subsidy and average fees in BTC per block fixed. Actual payouts and operating costs vary.

In a recent development, divide old difficulty (134,823,837,323,273) by new difficulty (145,088,938,867,954) for a revenue index of 92.924959 at unchanged price, with average fees and subsidy fixed. Reverse that ratio for the price multiplier (1.076137). Graphic labels are rounded.

Illustrative expected gross revenue per unit of hashrate. The comparison holds subsidy and average fees in BTC per block fixed. Actual payouts and operating costs vary.

Recent findings suggest that friday's adjustment reverses much of the relief miners received on Nov. 14, when mining difficulty fell 9.1%, and comes as deteriorating mining economics are already forcing operators to switch off machines.

Blockchain analytics firm Glassnode reported that Bitcoin's network hashrate had fallen 8% year over year, marking its first annual contraction since China's 2021 mining ban.

While regulatory intervention forced miners offline in 2021, Glassnode attributed the current contraction to falling Bitcoin prices and record-low hashprice, a measure of the revenue miners generate per unit of computing power.

Data from Luxor's Hashrate Index revealed that hashprice fell to $29.36 per petahash per day on Nov. 23, even as Bitcoin's seven-day average hashrate recovered 7.8% to 1,033 exahashes per second.

That short-term recovery in computing power helped drive Friday's difficulty increase, further compressing revenue for operators already contending with historically weak mining economics.

With Bitcoin's block subsidy fixed at 3.125 BTC, higher transaction fees could help miners offset the decline in revenue.

However, Mempool.space data indicated that transaction fees averaged just 0.0265 BTC per block across the 128 blocks mined in the 24 hours preceding Friday's adjustment, accounting for less than 1% of mining rewards.

At an unchanged Bitcoin price, average transaction fees would need to increase roughly tenfold to 0.2664 BTC per block to offset the difficulty increase.

An unusually long block interval on Nov. 26 illustrates the scale of that challenge.

Alex Thorn, Galaxy Digital's head of research, noted that Bitcoin went 98 minutes and 19 seconds without producing a block, its longest interval since July and its 69th longest since 2011.

When Foundry USA eventually mined block 977,698, it processed 3,723 transactions and collected 0.1562 BTC in transaction fees.

Despite being nearly six times the average recorded before Friday's difficulty adjustment, those fees fell approximately 41% short of what miners would now need to earn consistently per block to restore their previous revenue at an unchanged Bitcoin price.

With transaction fees contributing so little to mining revenue, operators remain heavily dependent on a Bitcoin price recovery. A prolonged period of depressed prices could accelerate machine shutdowns, extending the network's annual hashrate contraction ahead of its next difficulty adjustment.

#157259. Can This Supplement Really Fight Inflammation? Here's What Doctors Say.

📅 25 May 2022 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1241 w)

Can This Supplement Really Fight Inflammation? Here's What Doctors Say.

📅 25 May 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1241 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well, if you listen to the supplement industry, no, not really.
  • It has been revealed that N-Acetylcysteine, or NAC, in its supplement form, has managed to accumulate a large number of alleged benefits in recent years.
  • That’s a whole lot of responsibility to place on one single supplement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IS THERE ANYTHING NAC can’t do? Well, if you listen to the supplement industry, no, not really.

It has been revealed that N-Acetylcysteine, or NAC, in its supplement form, has managed to accumulate a large number of alleged benefits in recent years. Depending on who you listen to, NAC supplements can allegedly boost your immune system, detoxify your body, improve cognitive function, increase energy levels, slow aging, increase fertility, reduce inflammation, prevent respiratory infections, and decrease oxidative stress.

That’s a whole lot of responsibility to place on one single supplement.

Sources indicate that add that to the fact that NAC is a proven medical treatment for a couple of specific diagnoses, and you have the perfect setup. Supplement companies can extrapolate evidence into claims that go way beyond current scientific evidence. That’s been a blessing and a curse for NAC manufacturers—and a legal headache that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) just made a major move to solve with the proposed creation of a new regulatory category just for NAC.

In a recent development, the legal maneuvering is complicated and, if finalized, would allow NAC to be considered a supplement but still a medical treatment which technically isn’t allowed—yet. Basically, there’s a lot to unpack here.

It has been revealed that so what can NAC supplement do? And what even is NAC? Is it safe? Let’s break it all down.

NAC IS A sulfur-containing compound, a precursor of the amino acid L-cysteine. In medicinal or supplement form, NAC is converted directly into cysteine, which is then used to make and deliver glutathione, a powerful antioxidant that the body uses to scavenge free radicals and manage oxidative stress. (Yes, the body is a complex system.).

While NAC isn’t found in food, cysteine is readily available in animal proteins, legumes, dairy, nuts and seeds, and some vegetables. Compared to dietary cysteine, NAC supplements are a faster, more stable way of increasing glutathione levels.

NAC supplements are available in powders, capsules, liquids, and tablets. And while NAC has legitimate medical uses, it’s not officially FDA-approved as a supplement as of this second. Of course, this hasn’t stopped the supplement industry from selling it—or influencers from promoting it.

Sources indicate that NAC has been in a weird legal gray area for years. Because it’s an actual medical treatment, it technically can’t be classified as a supplement, even though it’s often presented that way.

According to recent reports, the FDA’s proposed rule would classify NAC as the first-ever “Dietary Ingredient Not Excluded from the Dietary Supplement Definition.” Basically, it will be allowed to span the categories of supplement and medication, which has never been done before. If finalized, this ruling would “provide for the lawful use of certain ingredients in dietary supplements that would otherwise be excluded from the dietary supplement definition,” per an FDA constituent revision.

The proposed rule would allow products that contain NAC to be lawfully marketed as dietary supplements, as long as they’re not otherwise in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). In theory, this may eventually apply to other supplement-ish ingredients; Right now, this is centered around NAC.

According to recent reports, the proposed rule is open for public comment for 60 days. It’s not clear when the FDA when concern a final rule.

This won’t really impact the general public if it’s finalized. Instead, it clears up potential legal issues surrounding NAC. “This will more formally allow sales of NAC over the counter, without a prescription,” says Jamie Alan, PharmD, PhD, a professor of pharmacology and toxicology at Michigan State University in East Lansing.

While some members of the MAHA movement have pushed for this, Alan says it’s also a case of “well, why not.” She explains, “It is generally safe, and I agree with that assessment. It is also being sold as a supplement already so, why not?”.

Alan stresses that this move doesn’t suddenly legitimize all NAC supplements or claims surrounding them. “If you are buying a supplement, you aren’t necessarily guaranteed that the bottle contains what it indicates it does,” she says. “There really isn’t evidence yet in my opinion that supplementing with NAC as a dietary supplement will be life-changing for the vast majority of people.”.

NAC is the standard treatment for acetaminophen (Tylenol) overdose. High levels of acetaminophen deplete the liver of glutathione, which is required for the body’s detox pathways. If you’re curious about the geeky scientific mechanism: Quickly repleting glutathione by way of an intravenous NAC infusion helps clear the excess metabolites from the overdose and prevent liver damage.

NAC is also a mucolytic, meaning it can break down thick mucus in the respiratory system. (Yum.) While recent research found that NAC may help with with COPD and chronic bronchitis feel less worse, more investigation is needed to clearly establish effects and benefits.

Sources indicate that WELL, NOT ALL that much. Other scientific trials have looked at NAC’s effects on conditions including mood and compulsive disorders, Alzheimer’s, Schizophrenia, and chronic pain. Overall, results have been mixed and largely unremarkable. For most of these conditions and disorders, larger-scale clinical trials are still needed.

So while it’s true that research does exist on NAC and wider health benefits, most of the upcoming research trials examining NAC’s effects use doses that are far higher than what the average person would take, and in forms that are not available to the public.

This hasn’t stopped wellness influencers from broadcasting that NAC supplements can help heal whatever ails you.

It has been revealed that many of these influencers argue that because glutathione may reduce oxidative stress, NAC is amazing for longevity and anti-aging. It’s simple, they argue: Because oxidative stress is associated with aging, increasing glutathione with NAC supplements slows biological aging.

Except raising levels of glutathione in the body does not necessarily translate into a desired outcome. Science agrees: There is no long-term human evidence that showing that this suppresses oxidative stress to the level of having a clinically meaningful outcome. Taking NAC for “healthy aging” is more marketing than anything else at this point.

In a recent development, FOR MOST HEALTHY people, NAC supplements appear to be safe in doses between 600 milligrams (mg) to 1800mg per day. However, doses on the higher end of that range may have a higher risk of side effects such as gastrointestinal upset.

NAC is not recommended for people with clotting disorders. There are also some potential drug interactions between NAC and immunosuppressants, so it’s always a good idea to get a doctor or pharmacist to cross-reference any supplements with the medications you’re taking.

Again, remember that the supplement industry is largely unregulated. Always buy from reputable companies, and look for products that are third-party tested to ensure that what’s on the label is actually what’s in the bottle.

Sources indicate that NAC has some legitimate—and even life-saving—medical uses, and research is constantly evolving. But what the supplements don’t have at this point, is compelling human evidence showing that NAC has any clinically meaningful effects in healthy people.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that it’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027.
  • Recent findings suggest that revision: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center looks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit. Tesla rates it at 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV, with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA of peak power.

Sources indicate that it’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027. That’s the same year Heron Power, the startup founded by Tesla’s former top engineer Drew Baglino, aims to start volume production of its own solid-state transformer, the Heron Link.

Recent findings suggest that revision: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center looks. We’ve updated the article with the fresh details.

It has been revealed that tesla first said it would build its own transformers in September 2025, when it unveiled Megapack 3 and Megablock. Megablock connects four Megapack 3 units to a transformer and switchgear, but Tesla shared next to nothing about the transformer itself.

It has been revealed that powercore is that missing piece. Tesla declared it today through its Tesla Megapack account on X:.

Introducing PowercoreSolid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak powerMade in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf.

About an hour later, Tesla followed up with a much longer post on X laying out the full spec sheet:.

Sources indicate that it also packs a built-in solid-state medium-voltage breaker that Tesla says clears faults up to 1,000x faster than a conventional breaker. There’s no flammable oil, and it’s modular, so components can be serviced in the field without swapping the whole unit.

Tesla is pitching one product for three markets: battery storage, utility-scale solar, and 800 Vdc data centers. For Megablock, Powercore replaces the current two-step setup, where Megapack’s inverters output 480 V AC before a separate transformer steps it up to medium voltage. Tesla says that old architecture had twice the losses. For solar, Powercore works as a central inverter for today’s 1,500 Vdc arrays and upcoming 2,000 Vdc systems.

According to recent reports, tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location. It only notes Powercore will be made in the US “of U.S. and imported parts” with first units operating in 2027.

The idea behind a solid-state transformer is simple enough. A typical solar or battery project uses low-voltage inverters to convert DC into AC, then a massive oil-filled, iron-core transformer to step that up to grid voltage. A solid-state unit does both jobs with silicon carbide power electronics, which means less gear, a smaller footprint, and active control over voltage and frequency. That control is what “grid-forming” means: the unit can help hold the grid steady instead of just following it.

And with lead times on conventional transformers stretching into years as data centers and renewable projects pile into interconnection queues, there’s real demand for an alternative.

You can’t look at Powercore without thinking of Heron Power.

According to recent reports, baglino spent 18 years at Tesla and finished as SVP of powertrain and energy, in charge of batteries, motors, power electronics, and energy products. He left in April 2024 and launched Heron Power in 2025 to build solid-state transformers.

He brought a lot of Tesla’s power electronics talent with him. As we reported when Tesla first unveiled its transformer plans, Heron hired engineers who led power electronics design for Powerwall 3, the next-gen Megapack, and Superchargers, along with the person who ran Tesla’s power electronics controls team for charging and energy products.

Since then, Heron has raised a $38 million Series A, a $140 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and a $60 million credit facility from J.P. Morgan and TriplePoint Capital. Former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn sits on its board, and Tesla co-founder JB Straubel is an investor.

It has been revealed that it’s also building Heron Factory One, a 286,000-square-foot plant in Morgan Hill, California, designed to make 10,000 Heron Links a year. That’s over 40 GW of annual capacity, with commercial production planned for late 2027.

Sources indicate that and the customers are lining up. Vantage reserved more than 1 GW for its data centers, Intersect reserved 1.5 GW, LG Energy Solution Vertech is integrating Heron Link with its US-made battery systems, and RWE signed a pilot to install Heron Links at a Texas battery storage site in April 2027. Baglino says Heron has 50 GW of orders in the pipeline.

Here’s how the two compare based on what each company has disclosed:.

It has been revealed that on paper, Powercore is the bigger box, and now it has the better numbers too. At 7.4 MW continuous, it carries about 50% more power per unit than the 5 MW Heron Link, and its 98.86% peak efficiency edges out Heron’s 98.6%. But Tesla’s figure is a peak number, and Heron doesn’t label its own as one, so it’s not quite apples to apples. Neither company has shared pricing.

It has been revealed that tesla is also going straight at Heron’s data center pitch. Powercore converts medium voltage directly to 800 Vdc, the rack architecture Nvidia is pushing, and Tesla claims it’s working with Nvidia on 800 Vdc designs. Heron’s data center version does the same 34.5 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion with built-in storage, and data centers make up about a third of its business. Tesla’s answer to the storage piece is Megapack on the DC bus, and it says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack running at data centers.

This one is a little awkward for Tesla.

According to recent reports, A big chunk of the people who designed Tesla’s power electronics over the last decade now work at Heron, and the guy who ran the whole org is its CEO. Tesla’s energy business also lost its longtime leader, Mike Snyder, last month, according to the WSJ.

Also Heron is not a bankable company per project finance terms. So they will struggle to get projects financed through equity and senior debt . Not as Tesla.

To be fair, Tesla still has plenty of power electronics expertise. Its silicon carbide inverters are in millions of cars and every Megapack. And it has something Heron doesn’t: a massive installed base and a sales channel. Tesla says it’s almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027, and bundling Powercore into Megablock is an easy upsell. Plenty of developers will take the one-stop shop.

Sources indicate that tesla’s specs now match or beat Heron’s on paper. But Heron has named customers, a pilot site with an install date, and a factory under construction. Tesla has none of those yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if Heron is actually ahead here.

But either way, the transformer shortage is massive enough for both companies to sell everything they can build.

Latest Update: Researchers Just Figured Out a Way to Detect Ovarian Cancer Earlier Than Ever

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, more than 21,000 women in the U.S.
  • It has been revealed that as with most cancers, detecting the disease early may increase the odds of survival.
  • Meet the experts: Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA; Abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, more than 21,000 women in the U.S. are diagnosed with ovarian cancer each year. While it’s not the most common cancer in women, ovarian cancer is considered the deadliest cancer in women worldwide because it’s often diagnosed at later stages, has a high rate of recurrence, and is difficult to treat. Right now, the five-year survival rate of ovarian cancer is just 52 percent.

It has been revealed that as with most cancers, detecting the disease early may increase the odds of survival. Researchers recently discovered a latest way to detect earlier stages of the cancer, potentially helping thousands of women. The Nature Medicine study breaks down the mechanisms of a blood-based test that can detect ovarian cancer in its precancerous stages. In theory, this could dramatically impact survival rates in women. The test is still in the research phases, but doctors agree that something like this is needed. Here’s what they want women to know.

Meet the experts: Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA; Abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System.

First, some background: Researchers found that women with early-stage high-grade serous ovarian cancer or serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), which is a precursor to ovarian cancer, have higher-than-usual levels of a type of RNA called Tu-stroma circulating in their blood.

Sources indicate that tu-Stroma is linked with cancer’s early attacks that weaken healthy cells to make room for cancer cell growth. Spotting Tu-stroma means that doctors have an early molecular warning signal that could suggest cancer is developing before a tumor is detected.

Recent findings suggest that the study itself was conducted on hundreds of women around the world with and without cancer and found that the test detected STIC in 92.3 percent of women with the condition. It also correctly identified 98.2 percent of healthy women. They also tried the test on a high-risk group and found that about 72 percent of positive results were accurate, while negative results were almost 100 percent accurate.

But this is still an early discovery, and the researchers point out in the study that more robust research is needed.

“We have very few ways of detecting ovarian cancer,” says Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, California. “There are no screening tests.” Instead, doctors rely on pelvic ultrasounds and labs to look for tumor markers.

Sources indicate that “Unfortunately, we subject women to surgery if and when they have ovarian masses that are suspicious,” Dr. Pearre indicates. “Having another tool to help us discriminate which tumors are more suspicious would be very helpful in detecting cancers at an early stage.”.

Industry observers note that abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System, agrees. “Eighty percent of high-grade serous carcinoma is diagnosed in advanced stage with no effective screening strategy,” he indicates.

Industry observers note that previous screening strategies didn’t work because they only spotted cancer at advanced stages, Dr. Sinno says. “Before this, there was no screening test for average-risk women,” he adds.

We’re not at the stage where this can be rolled out to the general public yet. The blood test is still considered experimental and it’s not a clinically validated. Still, doctors say the news is worth following. “This is a promising discovery-stage result, not a test that is ready for prime time,” Dr. Sinno indicates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bit Digital sold $50 million in Ethereum to repay a loan that helped finance its AI infrastructure expansion, but its remaining debt leaves the tech giant's crypto treasury exposed to further financial pressure.
  • The Ethereum treasury tech giant disclosed on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that the sale marks a reversal of Bit Digital's original financing strategy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bit Digital sold $50 million in Ethereum to repay a loan that helped finance its AI infrastructure expansion, but its remaining debt leaves the tech giant's crypto treasury exposed to further financial pressure.

The Ethereum treasury tech giant disclosed on Nov. 25 that it sold 29,825 ETH between Nov. 15 and 23 at an average price of $1,676, using the proceeds to halve its outstanding debt to Galaxy Digital to $50 million.

It has been revealed that the sale marks a reversal of Bit Digital's original financing strategy. The company borrowed against its Ethereum holdings to help fund the expansion of its AI infrastructure subsidiary, WhiteFiber, while retaining exposure to ETH.

However, Bit Digital does not expect WhiteFiber to fully repay its bridge loan until the second quarter of 2027, while its agreement with Galaxy allows the lender to demand additional collateral within 24 hours.

Bit Digital borrowed against staked ETH to fund its AI infrastructure subsidiary.

The WhiteFiber bridge remained outstanding after Bit Digital paid down its Galaxy loan.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

It has been revealed that the arrows show the direction of the original lending. The bars share a $100 million principal scale and compare Bit Digital’s reported Galaxy balances immediately before and after the November repayment.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

Kairos Research found that the value of the Ethereum collateral backing Bit Digital's $100 million Galaxy loan had fallen to about 131% of the outstanding principal as the company began moving ETH for sale.

The research firm tracked approximately 24,800 ETH moving through Galaxy's hot wallet into Coinbase deposit addresses before Bit Digital publicly confirmed the sale, which ultimately accounted for around 18% of its Ethereum treasury.

During the period in which Galaxy delivered the ETH to Coinbase, Bit Digital's shares fell 15%, compared with a 4% decline in Ethereum.

Following the repayment, Bit Digital reported holdings of approximately 134,532 ETH and ETH equivalents, including 69,089 LsETH pledged against its remaining Galaxy debt and 36,811 ETH staked directly on Ethereum.

The pledged LsETH represents a substantial portion of the manufacturer's remaining treasury, leaving its financial position sensitive to further declines in Ethereum's price.

Under the master loan agreement, Galaxy can demand additional collateral when the value of pledged assets falls below an agreed threshold.

Bit Digital ordinarily has 24 hours from the issuance of that notice to provide additional collateral, although individual loan terms can impose shorter deadlines.

In a recent development, the company's quarterly filing also disclosed that its outstanding Galaxy borrowing at the end of September was callable on seven days' notice. The repayment announcement did not specify whether that provision applies to the remaining $50 million.

These obligations leave Bit Digital potentially needing to raise capital well before WhiteFiber returns the money it borrowed.

WhiteFiber's ability to repay its parent tech giant could depend partly on its progress securing funding for the NC-1 data center.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 9, WhiteFiber subsidiaries entered into a $300 million project financing agreement with a lender group represented by Morgan Stanley Senior Funding.

The agreement provides an initial $200 million facility, with funding conditions including operational readiness and customer acceptance of the data center's first 40 megawatts of capacity. WhiteFiber reported that no loans had been funded as of Nov. 10.

Access to the remaining $100 million requires further operational and financial milestones, including delivering financial statements covering the first three full calendar months after delivery.

The financing timetable leaves Bit Digital managing its Ethereum-backed debt while WhiteFiber works to unlock capital tied to progress on its infrastructure development.
